question: Achilles runs ten times as fast as a tortoise that starts 100 metres ahead. How far does Achilles run before drawing level?
answer: About 111 metres. Zeno's stages are 100 metres, then 10, then 1, then 0.1, and so on; they add up to 111.1 recurring, or 1,000/9. Quicker: Achilles gains 9 metres on every 10 he runs, so the 100-metre gap closes after 1,000/9 metres. By then the tortoise has crawled just over 11 metres.
move: Endless stages can sum to a finite total; add them before despairing.
ask: Which endless chore of mine is actually a finite total I never added up?
trap: Infinitely many stages feel as if they must take forever.
source: Russell, Our Knowledge of the External World
reference: Russell, Our Knowledge of the External World, lecture 6, Open Court, 1914
